# Zoning & Development Analysis: 1500 W Wilson Ave, Uptown

**PIN:** 14171060250000 | **Community Area:** Uptown (CA-3) | **Ward:** 47 (Ald. Matthew J. Martin)

---

## 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **B1-2** — Neighborhood Shopping District, with a density designation of "-2." This comes directly from the City's official GIS zoning layer. You can verify it at the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

> **Confidence:** High — this is a live GIS query from the city's authoritative system.

## 2. Residential Uses: Apartments Above & On Ground Floor

**Above ground floor:** B1 districts are closely related to B2 in the Business/Commercial district family. Per [1], the B2 district explicitly "permits residential dwelling units on or above the ground floor" — B1 is the more restrictive neighborhood shopping district. Under the Chicago Zoning Ordinance, **B1 districts permit residential dwelling units above (but not on) the ground floor** as of right. The ground floor is reserved for commercial/retail uses in B1 districts.

**Ground-floor residential:** Ground-floor dwelling units are **not permitted as of right** in B1 districts. The B3 district allows residential above the ground floor [1], and conversion of ground-floor commercial to residential requires Zoning Administrator approval under [4]. A rezoning to B2 or B3 would open more residential options.

> **Confidence:** Moderate-to-high on above-ground residential being permitted; moderate on ground-floor prohibition — the code chunks retrieved focus on B2/B3 and R districts. You should confirm B1-specific use table provisions directly with the Department of Planning and Development (DPD) or in the full Title 17 use tables.

## 3. Key Bulk & Density Standards

The "-2" density designation governs your floor area ratio and height envelope. The relevant framework is [4] (bulk and density in B/C districts). **I was not able to retrieve the specific B1-2 FAR cap, maximum height, or minimum lot area per unit table rows from the code chunks provided** — the retrieved sections show the FAR table structure for B/C districts generally but do not display the actual numeric cells for B1-2.

What the code does establish:

- **Minimum lot area per unit:** Applies in R districts per [3]; in B districts the applicable standard is found in the B-district bulk table under [4]. The "-2" designation sets both the FAR ceiling and the density limit — but the numeric values require the full table from § 17-3-0403-A and § 17-3-0402.
- **FAR increase for transit-served locations:** Under [4], projects in **B-3 and C-3** districts within 2,640 feet of a CTA or Metra rail station may increase their maximum FAR — but this FAR boost is written specifically for B-3 and C-3, **not B-1**. A B1-2 parcel would need a Type 1 Zoning Map Amendment or Planned Development approval to access the higher FAR [4].
- **Setbacks:** B district setbacks are governed by § 17-3-0406 (not fully retrieved here). No front setback is explicitly required in most B districts, but side and rear setbacks depend on adjacency to residential zones.

> **How to verify:** Pull the full bulk tables from § 17-3-0402 (density/lot area) and § 17-3-0403-A (FAR by district) at [Chicago Municipal Code online](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/chicago/latest/chicago_il/0-0-0-2497). Contact DPD's Zoning Help Desk at (312) 744-5777 for a formal pre-application meeting.

> **Confidence:** Low on specific numeric values — the retrieved chunks did not include the B1-2 table rows. Do not rely on this analysis alone for design parameters.

(137 units). Any new residential development here will be subject to ARO affordability requirements [4].

**Transit-served location:** Per [2], new construction in B and C districts within **2,640 feet of a CTA or Metra rail station entrance** must satisfy specific criteria under § 17-3-0308. This parcel is 0.44 miles (~2,323 feet) from Montrose (Brown Line) and 0.4 miles from Ravenswood Metra — **both within the 2,640-foot threshold**, triggering transit-served location standards [2].

Additionally, because this is within a community preservation area and near transit, **newly established detached houses and two-flats are prohibited** in B and C districts under [2].

## 5. Parking Requirements & Transit Reductions

The code chunks retrieved do not include the specific parking tables for B1-2 districts (those appear in § 17-10-0200 and § 17-10-0102-B of Title 17). However, the ordinance establishes that:

- Projects in **transit-served locations** (within 2,640 feet of CTA/Metra rail) must comply with § 17-10-0102-B standards [2], which under the **Connected Communities Ordinance** typically allow **reduced or eliminated parking minimums** near transit.
- The TOD overlay (both CTA and Metra) confirmed on this parcel further supports parking reductions under the Connected Communities framework.

> **How to verify:** Review § 17-10-0102-B and the parking tables at § 17-10-0200 in the full Municipal Code. DPD's Zoning Help Desk can confirm the applicable reduction for your specific use mix.

> **Confidence:** Moderate — TOD eligibility is confirmed; the precise numerical reduction requires the full parking tables not retrieved here.
